s.d: a table computer from Apple Inc
A lightweight low-power tablet computer of a particular range from Apple Inc.
x: He was watching a movie on his iPad.
“This is before everyone had [geographic information system] mapping, before iPads, iPhones, laptops, Google,” he says. “This is doing research way back with a hammer and a chisel.”

ipecac.e: Contraction of ipecacuanha, from Portuguese ipecacuanha, from Old Tupi ypekakûãîa, from ypeka (“duck”) + akûãîa (“penis”).

s.d: a medicinal drug used to evoke vomiting (especially in cases of drug overdose or poisoning)
(uncountable) The dried rhizome and roots of either of two tropical American plants (Cephaelis acuminata and Cephaelis ipecacuanha) of the madder family used especially as a source of emetine.
(uncountable) An emetic and expectorant drug that contains emetine and is prepared from ipecac especially as a syrup for use in treating accidental poisoning.
(uncountable) The shrub that produces ipecac (Cephaelis ipecacuanha), native to Brazil and cultivated elsewhere.

iphone.e: From i- + phone. Many Apple products have an i- prefix in their names.

s.d: a smartphone designed and marketed by Apple Inc.
A smartphone of a series produced by Apple, which typically combine a camera phone, PDA, multimedia player, and wireless communication device.
x: His mom bought him an IPhone for his 11th birthday.
This concept puts the curve back on the iPhone 5 with a silhouette that's reminiscent of a banana phone.

s.d: Any knockoff or similar high-end smartphone; through trademark genericization.

ipse dixit.e:
Borrowed from Latin ipse dīxit (“he himself said it”), calque of Ancient Greek αὐτὸς ἔφα (autòs épha).
Originally used by the followers of Pythagoreanism, who claimed this or that proposition to be uttered by Pythagoras himself. Extended during the Middle Ages to the statements of Aristotle, and more famously used in such contexts.

s.d: an unsupported dogmatic assertion
(uncountable) A dogmatic and unproved proposition or dictum that is accepted solely on the authority of someone who is known to have asserted it.
x: To, avoid, therefore, all Imputation of laying down a Rule for Poſterity, founded only on the Authority of ipſe dixit; for which, to ſay the Truth, we have not the profoundeſt Veneration; […]

s.d: (uncountable) An authority who makes such an assertion.

ipsedixitism.e: From Latin ipse dīxit (“he himself said it”, used in the Middle Ages in reference to Aristotle) + -ism. Coined in the late 18th century by Jeremy Bentham.

s.d: an unsupported dogmatic assertion
An unfounded, false and dogmatic assertion; an ipse dixit.
(uncountable) The practice of making such assertions.
on or relating to the same side (of the body)

ipso facto.e: Borrowed from Latin ipsō factō (“by the fact itself”).

s.d: Being such by itself, or by its own definition; inherent.
x: Is not the reading of another's diary an ipso facto act of voyeurism?

s.d: by the fact itself
x: ipso facto, her innocence was established
